Assumptions used in Application of the Models to the Sarpy Creek Area
Consideration of construction of an SNG plant is in very preliminary stages and, therefore, various plant parameters used for this study were hypothetical. The plant parameters were assumed identical to those listed in the Northern Great Plains Resource Program (NGPRP) Atmospheric Aspects Work Group report and are reproduced here in Table 0-1. For all calculations within this report the plant was assumed operating at 100 percent capacity on a year round basis.
The plant was assumed located in Sarpy Creek Valley at an elevation of 3300 feet between the two tracts, south of the current administration building. Terrain is roughly 300 feet above the valley floor in all directions to a distance of about 10 kilometers away from the hypothetical plant location. It was assumed that the Little Wolf Mountains form an arc 16 kilometers away north-northeast to south-scutheast of the hypothetical plant and rise 1200 feet above the plant site floor. These terrain effects have been incorporated in all calculations.
Long-Term Modeling Assumptions
Meteorological data recorded for one year at Colstrip, Montana were used to obtain frequency distribution of dispersion conditions by wind
